title: Anna: Name Meaning, Origin & Personality
summary: Anna is a timeless and graceful name cherished across the globe for centuries. Its enduring appeal lies in its simple beauty and rich historical background.
origin: Anna is derived from the Hebrew name Hannah, meaning grace or favor. It entered the classical world through the Greek and Latin translations of ancient texts, where it quickly spread across Europe. The name has ancient royal roots and has been borne by queens, saints, and literary heroines throughout history. Today, Anna remains a beloved classic across Europe, the Americas, and parts of Asia, celebrated for its cross-cultural fluency and effortless elegance.
personality: Anna is often associated with a warm, gentle, and dependable nature. People with this name are frequently perceived as creative, thoughtful, and deeply compassionate friends who bring harmony to group settings. There is a quiet strength and resilience tied to the name, suggesting someone who is both adaptable and grounded. Popular perception views an Anna as intelligent and articulate, possessing a natural charm that makes others feel instantly welcome and valued in her presence.
popularity: Anna is a truly global name that has enjoyed remarkable and steady popularity for generations. It frequently ranks near the top of baby name lists throughout Europe, spanning from Scandinavia to Eastern Europe and the Mediterranean. In North America and many English-speaking regions, it maintains a strong, classic presence without ever feeling dated, beloved by parents seeking a traditional yet fresh-sounding choice for their newborn daughters.

faq.q: Is Anna considered a classic name?
faq.ans: Yes, Anna is one of the ultimate classic names, having remained in continuous use across many cultures for centuries. Its simple structure ensures it never goes out of style.

faq.q: What is the difference between Anna and Hannah?
faq.ans: Anna and Hannah share the same Hebrew root meaning grace. Hannah is the older traditional form, while Anna arrived via Greek and Latin translations.

faq.q: Does Anna have many international variations?
faq.ans: Indeed, almost every European language has its own beloved version of the name. Variations range from Ana in Spanish and Portuguese to Anouk in French and Dutch.

faq.q: Is Anna easy to pronounce in multiple languages?
faq.ans: One of the greatest strengths of Anna is its phonetic simplicity. It is easily recognized, spelled, and pronounced across dozens of different languages and cultures.
